TS Fitter API

This is the module that handles the loss function, gradient calculation, hessian calculation, and parameter generation

class inverse_thomson_scattering.model.TSFitter.TSFitter(cfg: Dict, sas, dummy_batch)Source

This class is responsible for handling the forward pass and using that to create a loss function

Parameters:

  • cfg – Configuration dictionary

  • sas – TODO

  • dummy_batch – Dictionary of dummy data

construct_bounds()Source

This method construct a bounds zip from the upper and lower bounds. This allows the iterable to be reconstructed after being used in a fit.

Args:

Returns:

smooth(distribution: Array) → ArraySource

This method is used to smooth the distribution function. It sits right in between the optimization algorithm that provides the weights/values of the distribution function and the fitting code that uses it.

Because the optimizer is not constrained to provide a smooth distribution function, this operation smoothens the output. This is a differentiable operation and we train/fit our weights through this.

Parameters:

distribution

Returns:

weights_to_params(input_weights: Dict, return_static_params: bool = True) → DictSource

This function creates the physical parameters used in the TS algorithm from the weights. The input these_params is directly modified.

This could be a 1:1 mapping, or it could be a linear transformation e.g. “normalized” parameters, or it could be something else altogether e.g. a neural network

Parameters:

  • these_params

  • return_static_params

Returns:

vg_loss(weights: Dict, batch: Dict)Source

This is the primary workhorse high level function. This function returns the value of the loss function which is used to assess goodness-of-fit and the gradient of that value with respect to the weights, which is used to update the weights

This function is used by both optimization methods. It performs the necessary pre-/post- processing that is needed to work with the optimization software.

Parameters:

  • weights

  • batch

Returns:
